iran.headline: Post-Khamenei succession crisis unresolved; Hormuz threat posture and IRGC command continuity remain active risk vectors
iran.summary: Following the reported killing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in Operation Epic Fury, Iran's Assembly of Experts faces an unprecedented succession process with no clear consensus candidate as of early 2026 reporting. Mojtaba Khamenei (the Supreme Leader's son) and IRGC-aligned figures including parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf represent competing power centers, while IRGC command continuity and retaliatory posture toward Gulf states and US assets remain the dominant near-term risk. The Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 20% of global oil supply transits, remains a potential retaliation chokepoint with IRGC naval forces capable of mine-laying and harassment operations.

oracle_ellison.headline: Oracle carries $100B+ debt load post-capital raise; Ellison personal guarantee on WBD acquisition adds compounding balance-sheet stress
oracle_ellison.summary: Oracle reported Q3 FY2026 earnings on approximately February 28, 2026, following a $45–50 billion capital raise in early 2026 to fund Stargate AI infrastructure commitments, pushing total debt obligations above $100 billion. Separately, Larry Ellison's reported ~$40.4 billion personal guarantee backing son David Ellison's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery via Paramount creates cross-collateral exposure that bond markets and rating agencies are tracking. An Ohio Carpenters Pension bondholder lawsuit adds litigation risk to what is already one of the most leveraged balance sheets in enterprise tech.

arkansas_datacenter.headline: Arkansas ballot preemption ruling and utility rate capture acts establish replicable template for state-level democratic accountability erosion
arkansas_datacenter.summary: The Arkansas Supreme Court's Good Day Farm ruling established precedent limiting citizen ballot initiative power, functioning as a structural preemption mechanism that compounds with Acts 373 and 548 — legislation enabling utility rate capture favorable to large industrial power consumers including hyperscale datacenter operators. Over $17 billion in datacenter capital has been directed toward Arkansas in part due to this regulatory environment, with Google and AVAIO among significant deployments, and L3Harris's Camden facility representing defense-industrial convergence. The proposed DATA Act of 2026 and CREU designation would allow federal energy bypass, further insulating these deployments from state and local democratic oversight.
